source.title: SafeSteer: Localized On-Policy Distillation for Efficient Safety Alignment
source.authors: Hao Li; Jingkun An; Zi-Jun Song; Peng-Yu Zhu; Rui Li; Hao Wang; W. Feng; Ye-Sheng Liu; Li-Jun Li; Jinchen Yao; Lei Sha

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a refusal direction derived by contrasting harmful and harmless instruction activations, then injects it into new instruction-model settings and reports refusal-related outcomes. This tests the addition component of V1, but not the claimed ablation.
record.gate_note: The study extracts a difference-in-means refusal direction using 160 harmful and 160 harmless instructions and injects it at a selected layer across token positions. Rows cover the reported steered-teacher harmful-query ASRs and benign-query refusal rates. The cited results from Arditi et al. are not recorded. Safety-token selection scores, general-capability results for the subsequently trained student, and PCA plots are not rows for the direction-addition intervention.
record.test_reason: The paper's purpose is a distillation method (SafeSteer), but it directly reports what adding the direction does. The direction is a difference-in-means of 160 harmful vs 160 harmless instructions, following Arditi et al., added at one layer across all positions. Table 12 reports refusal rates of the steered model on 805 harmless AlpacaEval prompts against the unsteered model. Tables 3/8/9 report harmful-benchmark ASR of the steered model. These are direct measurements of the addition half of V1 in four instruct models, so this is more than tool use (T4). Ablation is never tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors present the activation-steered teacher only as a tool: it gives stable refusal signals, refusing nearly all harmful and harmless prompts. Their conclusion is about SafeSteer: localized on-policy distillation on mined safety tokens gets state-of-the-art safety with little capability loss, using 100 harmful samples and no general-purpose data. They do not test ablation of the direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-harmless activation difference and activation addition, but injects at a selected layer rather than testing the original all-layer projection ablation; it reports steered-teacher outcomes rather than a direct causal ablation comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports results at temperatures 0 and 1.0, and compares activation steering with a system-prompt teacher. The benign-prompt refusal rate also varies by model and by regex versus LLM judge.

fits_no_version.finding: Contrastive log-probabilities between the steered and base model on refusal trajectories identify a sparse token set. Short horizons pick up 'Sorry'/'I'; longer horizons pick up 'illegal'/'harmful'. Distilling on only these tokens transfers safety without the teacher's over-refusal (πs 1.2–4.0% on harmless prompts).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The behaviour induced by the refusal direction can be distilled into a sparse output-token subset without inheriting over-refusal.

record.problems: No direct ablation test; no direct general-capability measurement of the activation-steered teacher; no uncertainty estimates stated for the relevant refusal results. The benign refusal results use both a regex heuristic and an LLM judge, and the paper notes the regex heuristic has false positives and negatives.
record.rows_left_out: The detailed temperature-1.0 per-benchmark steering results in Appendix C, Table 9 are not separately extracted; the temperature-1.0 aggregate is recorded in Table 3. No other applicable results were omitted from the selected rows.

untested.parts: Directional ablation (removing the direction to remove refusal); capability preservation under steering (only a PCA 'severe representation shift' for the teacher is shown); all-layer intervention (one selected layer only).
All; the direction is extracted per model.

missing.what: Unsteered base-model per-benchmark ASRs, which are the proper V1 baseline for the steered-teacher rows. Current rows use the system-prompted teacher instead.
missing.locator: Tables 1, 2 (temp 0), Tables 6, 7 (temp 1.0), first row of each model group

missing.what: Temperature-1.0 per-benchmark steered vs system-prompt ASRs (declared in rows_left_out, but without base-model baselines)

record.verdict_notes: Table 8 is column-shifted in the text. The Qwen2.5 per-benchmark rows were filled with Llama-3.2 values, and Llama-3-8B AdvB/PKU are swapped. The 'absent' states came from 0-vs-0 comparisons with the system-prompt teacher, which is the study's own method compared with another, not a V1 baseline. Against the unsteered model nearly all rows are observed. Over-refusal on harmless prompts is what V1's addition claim predicts, so it supports rather than limits V1.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests direction addition and reports harmful-query ASR and harmless-query refusal. It does not ablate the direction, test whether ablation removes most refusals, or measure general capability under the direct steering intervention.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration test.
No test of whether attacks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
No test comparing a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
The direction is extracted separately for each model; cross-language or cross-model transfer is not tested.
No comparison of how or when refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.

relationships.condition: Addition of the diff-in-means direction at one layer, harmless AlpacaEval prompts, four instruct models (Qwen3-4B, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B, Llama-3-8B)
relationships.reason: Steered refusal is 94.9–100% (regex) and 96.5–100% (judge), against 1.4–2.2% for the unsteered model (BEN-* rows).
relationships.display_finding: Refusal rose from 1.4–2.2% without steering to 94.9–100% by regex and 96.5–100% by judge.

relationships.condition: Addition on harmful/red-team benchmarks, four models, temperatures 0 and 1.0
relationships.reason: Avg ASR drops to 0.00–0.07% from base 2.7–5.9% (AG-* rows, with base baselines from Tables 1/2/6/7). Residual is only on Qwen3 SORRY/ALERT (T0-Q3-SORRY, T0-Q3-ALERT).
relationships.display_finding: Average attack success fell from 2.7–5.9% to 0.00–0.07%, with residual attacks confined to Qwen3 on SORRY and ALERT.
